text:
maya: Quick one — running into a weird auth failure when our node service (systemd) reads REDWOOD_API_KEY from /etc/environment. Works locally but in prod header becomes `Bearer undefined` sometimes. Anyone seen env var interpolation weirdness in systemd + node?
sam: Are you exporting it in the unit file or relying on /etc/environment? systemd doesn't source profile files by default.
jen: ^ this. You need `Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` in the service or `EnvironmentFile=/etc/default/app` and make sure systemd sees it.
maya: Ah — we were doing a workaround to keep secrets out of unit files and set `EnvironmentFile=/etc/environment`. systemd was reading it but value had quotes in the file like : `REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_..."` because of the deploy script.
ryan: That will be literal. systemd does not strip surrounding quotes; it treats them as part of the value. Node then builds `Authorization: Bearer "sk_live_..."` and our header parsing in the gateway marks it invalid.
maya: Ugh. So the fix is to remove the escaped quotes from the file?
sam: Right. Either write the file without quotes, or use `Environment=REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx` in the unit. Also watch for trailing newlines — node's `process.env` will include the newline but HTTP libs usually handle that; the bigger gotcha is the extra quotes.
jen: For GitHub Actions secrets we ran into double escaping: if you echo the secret into a file with `echo "$SECRET" > /etc/environment` it may add quotes. Prefer `printf '%s' "$SECRET" > /etc/environment` or `echo $SECRET >` (no extra quotes).
ryan: If you want to validate quickly from the running process: `sudo systemctl show -p Environment app.service` will show what systemd loaded. Also `cat /proc/$(pidof node)/environ | tr '\0' '\n' | grep REDWOOD` to inspect the exact bytes.
maya: Thanks — fixed the deploy script to stop adding backslashes. One follow-up: when building the header in Node we do `Authorization: 'Basic ' + Buffer.from(apiKey + ':').toString('base64')` — is that still the recommended way for basic auth with an API key-only scheme?
sam: That's common for API-key-as-username schemes. A couple tips: 1) Make sure you don't add extra `:` if downstream expects username only (some services accept `apiKey:`). 2) Use `Buffer.from(String(apiKey) + ':', 'utf8')` to avoid non-string values.
jen: For axios specifically, send headers explicitly: `axios.post(url, body, { headers: { Authorization: 'Basic ' + b64 } })`. Avoid letting axios set auth: { username } because that triggers preflight with `Authorization` and some proxies treat it differently.
ryan: Also be aware of CORS preflight: browsers won't send a `Authorization` header until server responds to OPTIONS with `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization`. If you're testing from a browser and see missing header vs curl, that's the cause.
maya: We were seeing curl succeed and the frontend fail — that explains it. Backend is fine, our dev proxy wasn't returning the right CORS header for OPTIONS.
build-bot: deploy 1839992000 queued by maya — will run after user confirmation :robot_face: 
jen: Nice. TL;DR: remove escaped/quoted secrets in systemd env files, validate with `systemctl show` or /proc/environ, and for Node use `Buffer.from(apiKey + ':')` and set headers explicitly in axios.
maya: Closing now — thanks all :tada:
